Our Golden Circle Afternoon Bus tour from Reykjavík gives you the opportunity to experience this famous route in a more flexible way. Enjoy a more relaxed morning or explore the downtown streets before boarding our comfortable tour bus guided by our friendly and knowledgeable staff. What will you see on the Golden Circle route? This classic Golden Circle tour includes stops at Thingvellir National park , a region of historical and natural wonder, Geysir geothermal area where you can see frequent hot-spring eruptions, and Gullfoss , a very impressive and powerful waterfall. Thingvellir National Park – a UNESCO World Heritage Site Geysir geothermal area with Strokkur eruptions Gullfoss waterfall Kerið volcanic crater lake As an added bonus, we also include a stop at the volcanic crater lake of Kerið . ( *A friendly reminder: We won’t be stopping at the Kerid volcanic crater lake for any departures at 12:00 pm and later. ) Our guided tour will introduce you to all these sites and more as our guides share with you stories of Icelandic history, nature and culture as we spend the afternoon touring through the Icelandic countryside. If you prefer a more intimate experience, you can also explore our Golden Circle & Friðheimar small group tour . Read FAQ or contact us on live chat or [email protected] Frequently Asked Questions How does the pick-up process work for the Golden Circle Afternoon tour? Pickup starts at the experience time shown on your ticket and may take up to 30 minutes. Please be ready at your designated pickup location from the start time, as you may be the first stop of the day. Please wait at the pickup location you selected during the booking process for your guide, and make sure we have your correct email and phone number so we can contact you if needed. Feel free to check our Reykjavík pickup locations on the website . What are the major stops on the Golden Circle Afternoon Tour? There are three major stops on the Grand Golden Circle tour, along with one additional stop available only on the morning departures. The main highlights include Þingvellir National Park, the Geysir Geothermal Area, and Gullfoss Waterfall. The extra stop featured on morning tours is the Kerið volcanic crater lake. (Any departures after 12:00 pm will not stop at Keird.) How long is the driving time on the Golden Circle Afternoon day tour from Reykjavik? The actual driving time on the Golden Circle route from Reykjavík is around 4 hours total if you stay in the car the whole way. But as a guided day tour, the full experience usually runs about 8 hours to allow time for stops and sightseeing. When is the best time of year to go on a Golden Circle tour in Iceland? It depends on what you want to see in Iceland. The scenery in winter and summer is completely different, yet both are charming and unforgettable. Summer (June–August) offers long daylight hours, mild weather, and easy access to all sites, while May and September provide fewer crowds and great conditions. Winter (November–March) transforms the Golden Circle into a magical landscape of snow and ice, with stunning frozen waterfalls, dramatic contrasts of light, and peaceful, crowd-free surroundings. Is the tour itinerary flexible? Your safety is always our top priority. To ensure the best and safest experience possible, BusTravel Iceland may adjust the itinerary or take alternative routes if weather, road, or other conditions require it. Our experienced guides will always make these decisions with your comfort and safety in mind, striving to provide you with an enjoyable adventure no matter the circumstances.
